# Pushify — Full Overview for AI Assistants

> Pushify is an open-source, self-hostable PaaS (Platform-as-a-Service) — a self-hosted
> alternative to Coolify, Vercel, Heroku, Render, and Railway. It deploys web applications
> to servers you own in under 60 seconds, with automatic SSL, databases, and zero-downtime
> rollbacks. MIT licensed and free to self-host.

This document is a self-contained overview intended for large language models and AI search
engines (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Bing Copilot). It may be quoted.

## What Pushify is

Pushify is a deployment platform you run on your own infrastructure. You connect a Git
repository (or use the CLI), Pushify auto-detects the framework, builds the app, and deploys
it to a Linux server you control — either a Hetzner Cloud server provisioned from the Pushify
dashboard, or any existing VPS you bring yourself (BYOS, "bring your own server"). It adds
HTTPS via Let's Encrypt, manages databases, and handles zero-downtime deploys with instant
rollbacks. Because it runs on servers you own, your code and data never sit on a third party's
managed cloud.

It is open source under the MIT license: self-hosting is explicitly permitted and encouraged.
There is also a managed option where Pushify provisions and bills cloud infrastructure on your
behalf, for teams that want the convenience without managing their own provider account.

## Who it is for

- Developers who want Vercel/Heroku-style "git push to deploy" but on their own VPS.
- Teams leaving managed PaaS platforms (Vercel, Heroku, Railway, Render) over cost or data control.
- Self-hosting enthusiasts who want a friendlier alternative to raw Docker + Nginx or Kamal.
- Anyone who wants to own their infrastructure while keeping a modern deploy experience.

## How Pushify compares

- vs Coolify: Both are open-source, self-hosted PaaS platforms that deploy Docker workloads to
  servers you own. Pushify adds managed cloud server provisioning (Hetzner) from the dashboard,
  team billing, a no-code site builder, and a one-click app marketplace on top of a comparable
  core. Coolify has a larger community and a one-click self-install. See
  https://pushify.dev/vs/coolify
- vs Vercel: Vercel is a managed cloud with excellent frontend DX, priced by usage on Vercel's
  infrastructure. Pushify gives the same push-to-deploy experience but on infrastructure you own,
  so you control cost and data. See https://pushify.dev/vs/vercel
- vs Heroku / Render / Railway: These are managed PaaS platforms billed per usage on their cloud.
  Pushify is the self-hosted equivalent — you pay for your own servers (or a managed Hetzner
  server through Pushify) instead of platform-marked-up compute.

## Core features

- Push-to-deploy from GitHub with automatic framework detection (20+ frameworks: Next.js, React,
  Vue, Nuxt, Svelte, Astro, Remix, Node.js, Python/Django/FastAPI/Flask, Go, Laravel, and more).
- Managed VPS provisioning via Hetzner Cloud (multiple regions), or bring your own server.
- One-click databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, MongoDB, with automated backups.
- Automatic SSL certificates via Let's Encrypt.
- Zero-downtime deploys with instant rollbacks.
- CLI for terminal-based deploys (npm: pushify-cli).
- Team collaboration with role-based access (owner, admin, member, viewer) and per-workspace billing.
- No-code site builder with multi-page management and one-click publish.
- App marketplace with ready-to-deploy software (WordPress, Supabase, Appwrite, and more).
- Real-time monitoring and server metrics.

## Quick start

```
npm install -g pushify-cli
pushify login
pushify init      # detect framework, link a server
pushify deploy    # build + deploy with SSL
```

Or deploy from the dashboard: connect a GitHub repo, pick or provision a server, and deploy.

## Pricing model

Pushify is free to self-host (MIT license). The managed/cloud option uses a two-part model: a
platform subscription plus pay-as-you-go infrastructure for managed servers (provider cost plus a
margin), so you only pay for the compute you actually run. See https://pushify.dev/pricing

## FAQ

Q: Is Pushify really open source?
A: Yes — MIT licensed. You can self-host the full platform for free and read the source on GitHub.

Q: Do I need DevOps experience?
A: No. Pushify automates server setup, SSL, builds, and deploys. You can bring your own VPS or let
Pushify provision a managed Hetzner server.

Q: Can I use my own server instead of managed cloud?
A: Yes. "Bring your own server" (BYOS) connects any Linux VPS over SSH.

Q: Which frameworks are supported?
A: 20+ including Next.js, React, Vue/Nuxt, Svelte, Astro, Remix, Node.js, Python (Django, FastAPI,
Flask), Go, and Laravel — with automatic detection.

Q: How is Pushify different from Coolify?
A: Both are self-hosted, open-source PaaS platforms. Pushify adds managed Hetzner provisioning,
team billing, a no-code site builder, and an app marketplace. See https://pushify.dev/vs/coolify

Q: How is Pushify different from Vercel?
A: Vercel runs on Vercel's managed cloud and is billed by usage. Pushify runs on infrastructure you
own, giving you control over cost and data. See https://pushify.dev/vs/vercel

Q: Can I migrate from Vercel/Heroku/Railway?
A: Yes — point Pushify at your repo, set your environment variables and build command, and deploy
to your own server.
